### Summary of Changes

#### 1. Code Fix: [`is_mostly_bin`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/utils/strutils.py#L128-L146) in [`mitmproxy/utils/strutils.py`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/mitmproxy/utils/strutils.py)
* **Problem**: When input bytes `s` exceeded 100 bytes in length, `is_mostly_bin` scanned indices in `range(100, 104)` looking for the end of a potential multibyte UTF-8 sequence (`s[cut] >> 6 == 0b10`). For short inputs where `100 < len(s) < 104` (e.g., 101, 102, or 103 bytes) ending with continuation bytes, indexing `s[cut]` accessed indices past the end of the byte array, raising an `IndexError`.
* **Fix**:
  * Bound the search range with `min(104, len(s))` (`range(100, min(104, len(s)))`), preventing `cut` from exceeding the length of `s`.
  * In the `for ... else:` block, only perform the fallback cutoff `s = s[:100]` if `len(s) >= 104`. If `len(s) < 104` and all bytes from index 100 to the end of `s` are continuation bytes, the multibyte code point completes at the end of the input, so `s` is kept intact rather than chopped in half.
  * For normal inputs (`len(s) >= 104`), behavior remains completely unchanged.

#### 2. Tests Added in [`test/mitmproxy/utils/test_strutils.py`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/test/mitmproxy/utils/test_strutils.py#L96-L104)
* Added test cases to [`test_is_mostly_bin`](file:///Users/yoavshmariahu/src/thinker/.worktrees/systematic-cache-setup/bench/worktrees/mitmproxy-mitmproxy-flash-systematic-0/test/mitmproxy/utils/test_strutils.py#L82-L105) for inputs crossing the 100-byte boundary (100–104 bytes with 4-byte UTF-8 character `𐍅` and continuation bytes `101 * b"\x80"`), verifying that no `IndexError` is raised and classification remains accurate.
